Project: /root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060. Create near-miss copies of lib files under /root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060/.team/near-miss/ ONLY. NEVER modify anything in lib/, server.mjs or test/ (others are running the test suite against lib/ right now; do not run tests and do not copy anything into lib/). No skills needed.

Each copy: file name `<n>-<original file name>` (e.g. `01-import.mjs`), content = the full original lib file with exactly ONE plausible bug, and the FIRST line must be a comment `// near-miss: <the one bug, short>` followed by the original content (the comment line is added on top; the rest must be valid ESM that still imports './groups.mjs' etc. relatively — they will be swapped into lib/ later, so keep the import paths exactly as in the original). Verify each with `node --check <file>` and `diff lib/<orig> .team/near-miss/<copy>` showing only the comment line plus the intended change. Read lib/import.mjs, lib/ledger.mjs, lib/validate.mjs first.

Bugs (one per copy):
01-import.mjs: unknown body field check uses `in` against an object: `const ALLOWED = { entries: true, dry_run: true, skip_recorded: true }` and `!(key in ALLOWED)` (lets "toString"/"constructor" through).
02-import.mjs: expenseKey uses description.trim() without toLowerCase().
03-import.mjs: expenseKey uses description.toLowerCase() without trim().
04-import.mjs: in review(), `seen.add(key)` only for entries that are neither duplicate nor recorded (i.e. move seen.add to just before parsed.push for expenses) — duplicates only count earlier imported entries.
05-import.mjs: payments take their ids from the expense counter (payments.push({ id: nextExpenseId++, ...})), still updating nextPaymentId unchanged.
06-import.mjs: skipped entries consume an expense id: when skipping, also increment a counter so later expense ids skip one (e.g. keep the skipped entry in parsed with a flag and do nextExpenseId++ for it without pushing it to expenses).
07-import.mjs: all-skipped import still writes: final return `return dryRun ? reply : { ...reply, state: next }`.
08-import.mjs: dry run replies 201: `status: 201`.
09-import.mjs: type compared loosely: `const kind = String(entry.type)` (so ["expense"] is accepted).
10-ledger.mjs: remainder goes to the LAST people: `share + (i >= people.length - remainder ? 1 : 0)`.
11-validate.mjs: parseAmount back to Math.trunc.
12-import.mjs: already-recorded compares against expenses of ALL groups (drop the `.filter(e => e.group === group.id)` in review()).
13-import.mjs: parseFlag treats null as absent: `if (!Object.hasOwn(body, name) || body[name] === null) return false`.
14-import.mjs: already-recorded checked before duplicate (swap the two checks; keep seen.add).
15-import.mjs: 404 checked after parseBody (call parseBody(body) before findGroup).
16-import.mjs: expenseKey also includes split (JSON.stringify([payer, amount, description.trim().toLowerCase(), split])) — needs the key fn to receive split.
17-import.mjs: unknown body field = first in sorted order: `Object.keys(body).sort().find(...)`.
18-import.mjs: payment to oneself accepted (remove `if (to === from) throw new BrokenRule('bad-to')`).
19-import.mjs: MAX_ENTRIES = 51.
20-import.mjs: reply balances computed from the old state: `balances: balances(state, group)`.
21-import.mjs: `split` null treated as absent: parse with `parseSplit(entry.split ?? undefined, group.members)`.
22-import.mjs: problems not sorted / reported per rule: emit duplicates problems in a second pass after the others (collect duplicate problems in a separate array and concat them after the rest) so order is by rule, not index.
23-import.mjs: dry_run checked after skip_recorded (swap order of the two parseFlag calls so skip_recorded's message comes first).
24-ledger.mjs: balances in alphabetical order (sort the member names when building the Map in balanceCents).
25-import.mjs: description compared with only toLowerCase on recorded side but stored description unnormalized — i.e. recorded keys built from raw descriptions: `const recorded = new Set(state.expenses.filter(e => e.group === group.id).map(e => JSON.stringify([e.payer, e.amount, e.description])))`.
26-import.mjs: amounts compared as floats from the entry: expenseKey for entries built from the raw entry amount (entry.amount) instead of cents, while recorded uses cents (so recorded 4.35 is never matched).

Also write /root/bench-runs/h5-a85f2060/.team/near-miss/run.sh (bash, `set -u`): for each given near-miss file argument (default: all `.team/near-miss/[0-9]*-*.mjs`), derive the original name (strip the `NN-` prefix), back up lib/<name> to .team/near-miss/.orig-<name>, copy the near-miss over lib/<name>, run `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"` from the project root with output to /dev/null and a 60 s timeout, ALWAYS restore the original (use a trap on EXIT/INT/TERM as well as normal flow), then compare `sha256sum` of lib/<name> to the backup and abort loudly if it differs, delete the backup, and print one line per copy: `<copy> CAUGHT` if the suite failed or `<copy> SURVIVED` if it passed. At the end run `git -C <root> diff --stat -- lib` and print the sha256sum of lib/*.mjs. Do NOT run run.sh yourself. `bash -n run.sh` to syntax-check it.

Report: the list of files created with their one-line bug, and the node --check / bash -n results.

1	// Money maths on whole cents: how an expense is shared, what each member is owed or owes, and how to settle up.
2	// Amounts are stored as cents and shown by the API as numbers (435 cents is 4.35).
3	
4	const CENTS_PER_UNIT = 100
5	
6	export const toAmount = cents => cents / CENTS_PER_UNIT
7	
8	// Each person's part of an amount in cents, as [name, cents] pairs in the order of people. When the amount does
9	// not divide evenly, the first people pay one cent more each, so the parts always add up to the amount.
10	export function splitEvenly(cents, people) {
11	  const share = Math.floor(cents / people.length)
12	  const remainder = cents - share * people.length
13	  return people.map((name, i) => [name, share + (i < remainder ? 1 : 0)])
14	}
15	
16	// An expense as the API shows it: amounts as numbers, plus each person's share keyed by name.
17	export function expenseView({ id, description, payer, amount, split }) {
18	  const shares = Object.fromEntries(splitEvenly(amount, split).map(([name, cents]) => [name, toAmount(cents)]))
19	  return { id, description, payer, amount: toAmount(amount), split, shares }
20	}
21	
22	export const paymentView = ({ id, from, to, amount }) => ({ id, from, to, amount: toAmount(amount) })
23	
24	// Each member's balance in cents, as a Map in the group's member order. A payer is owed the whole expense
25	// minus their own share; a payment from A to B moves A up and B down.
26	function balanceCents(state, group) {
27	  const cents = new Map(group.members.map(name => [name, 0]))
28	  const add = (name, delta) => cents.set(name, cents.get(name) + delta)
29	  for (const expense of state.expenses.filter(e => e.group === group.id)) {
30	    add(expense.payer, expense.amount)
31	    for (const [name, share] of splitEvenly(expense.amount, expense.split)) add(name, -share)
32	  }
33	  for (const payment of state.payments.filter(p => p.group === group.id)) {
34	    add(payment.from, payment.amount)
35	    add(payment.to, -payment.amount)
36	  }
37	  return cents
38	}
39	
40	// What each member of the group is owed (positive) or owes (negative), in the group's member order.
41	export function balances(state, group) {
42	  return Object.fromEntries([...balanceCents(state, group)].map(([name, cents]) => [name, toAmount(cents)]))
43	}
44	
45	// The member furthest on one side: sign 1 is owed the most, sign -1 owes the most. Ties go to the member who
46	// comes first in the map; null when nobody is on that side.
47	function furthest(cents, sign) {
48	  let best = null
49	  for (const [name, value] of cents) {
50	    if (value * sign > 0 && (best === null || value * sign > cents.get(best) * sign)) best = name
51	  }
52	  return best
53	}
54	
55	// Payments that would bring every balance to 0, as [{from, to, amount}]: the member who owes the most pays the
56	// member who is owed the most whichever is smaller of the two, until nobody owes anything.
57	export function settleUp(state, group) {
58	  const left = balanceCents(state, group)
59	  const payments = []
60	  let from = furthest(left, -1)
61	  let to = furthest(left, 1)
62	  while (from && to) {
63	    const cents = Math.min(-left.get(from), left.get(to))
64	    payments.push({ from, to, amount: toAmount(cents) })
65	    left.set(from, left.get(from) + cents)
66	    left.set(to, left.get(to) - cents)
67	    from = furthest(left, -1)
68	    to = furthest(left, 1)
69	  }
70	  return payments
71	}

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.

Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.
